# Ternuxx

**Repository:** [`soobujmiah/ternuxx`](https://github.com/soobujmiah/ternuxx). Use ./tx from a source checkout or the installed tx command.

**বাংলা:** Pocket-এ mobile workstation তৈরির স্বাধীন project। Native Termux layer compatible tools ও Android-facing integration-এর সুযোগ দেবে; বিদ্যমান Ternux Debian PRoot layer Linux desktop, established workload ও configured GPU path দেবে। Hybrid mode দুটিকে নিরাপদ handoff দিয়ে এক workstation-এ যুক্ত করবে।

**English:** I want my phone to be a workstation I can carry in my pocket. I want native Termux and my existing Ternux PRoot setup to work together, so I can use each where it fits. Read [what I have in mind](docs/PRODUCT-VISION.md).

## Quick start

Run these commands in Native Termux from the checkout:

```sh
./tx help
./tx info
./tx tui
./tx web
```

`./tx mng center` opens the Native GTK management app when the desktop and GTK dependencies are installed. `./tx db` opens the existing Debian PRoot shell through Ternuxx’s first-party, managed command. It is distinct from a bare `db` alias that may still be defined in the user’s shell configuration; use `tx db` for validated display/audio/environment handoff. `./tx pgui` opens the existing Debian XFCE desktop: standalone on `:0` when Native GUI is stopped, or nested through Xephyr on `:2` inside Native `:1`. Installed Debian GUI apps are auto-listed in a separate Native XFCE **PRoot Apps** menu. Refresh after changing guest apps with `./tx mng papps sync`; launch by menu or `./tx mng app launch --desktop-id APP.desktop`. The four management clients use the shared service, though feature coverage still differs by client.

## Runtime boundaries

- Native Termux owns the core and remains usable without Debian PRoot.
- The existing Debian guest is optional and preserved. Standalone, selected-app and nested desktop routes have different qualification results.
- Hybrid handoffs select a provider/display/audio route explicitly. Full clean setup replay and end-to-end qualification remain open.

See [architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [client coverage](docs/architecture/CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md), and [current limits](docs/testing/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md). Graphics evidence is specific to the named runtime/workload; no inference or NPU support follows from a desktop draw.

## PRoot Apps menu

Native XFCE gets a separate **PRoot Apps** category built from the visible application entries installed in the existing Debian guest. Ternuxx refreshes these launchers when its Native desktop starts; after adding or removing a Debian app while the desktop is open, run `./tx mng papps sync`. Each menu item goes through the shared management service and opens the matching guest desktop entry. Unrecognized or shell-command entries are skipped, and conflicting user-owned launchers are preserved.

## Existing Debian setup

Inspect the Ternuxx provider record with `./tx proot setup status`. If this checkout has not recorded the existing Debian rootfs, run `./tx proot setup adopt-preview --user NAME`, review the identified guest and plan, then apply that exact plan with `./tx proot setup adopt --user NAME --yes --plan-id ID`. Adoption records the rootfs identity in private Native state and does not modify Debian. It does not yet install packages, migrate guest configuration, or reproduce a fresh Debian setup on a separate disposable rootfs. The prior standalone Ternux CLI retirement is recorded in [P4 runtime evidence](docs/evidence/2026-10-22-p4-legacy-cli-and-runtime-recheck.md). See [the setup status and limits](docs/INSTALLATION.md#existing-debian-provider).

## Development and verification

Implement from Native Termux over SSH 8022 and keep live deployment plus repository updates together. Preserve the active Termux/Codex PRoot session. The installed tx shim loads this checkout; GTK and installed service/boot helpers need separate identity/deployment checks.

The installer uses exact preview-bound transactions. Fresh Debian setup currently has fixture evidence and refuses an existing rootfs; the customized workstation is not yet reproducible from this repository alone. ## Brand and license status

**Ternuxx** is the product and repository name. The only public command is tx (./tx in a source checkout).

This repository is public, but it has no `LICENSE` file and GitHub reports no detected license. Earlier commits stated “PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 plus the Ternux commercial-use addendum” and referenced files that were never committed. That historical statement is unresolved and needs qualified legal review. Do not treat the code as open source, assume the missing addendum's terms, or add a replacement license until the owner resolves the history and approves a license. See the [commercial and legal readiness audit](docs/readiness/README.md).


### Ternuxx Management Center

Use tx tui for the keyboard interface, tx web for the local authenticated Web Console, or tx mng center for the installed Native GTK4 app. Install/rebuild GTK with tx mng center install. All use shared typed management services; [the capability matrix](docs/architecture/CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md) records current coverage and gaps.

tx web offers Android, an installed Native browser, installed Debian Firefox ESR, or Auto. Use tx web --browser auto to skip the menu. Android uses clipboard paste; Native/PRoot X11 attempts to fill the masked code field. If both handoffs fail, the default stops without printing the code; explicit private terminal fallback requires --show-secret-on-clipboard-failure.

The Web UI has numbered purpose-based navigation, readable results, fixed related actions and mobile quick controls. Feature availability and live running state are separate. Detailed responses remain collapsed; runtime logs use bounded fixed Ternuxx sources. The Android Activity policy is distinct from Linux desktop health. See [verification](docs/testing/README.md).

### Managed SSH service deployment

The native managed SSH service on port 8023 has preview-first start, stop, and restart controls in CLI/TUI/Web/GTK, plus a separate run-definition deployment workflow. `tx ssh restart` shows an exact plan and warns that connected 8023 clients may disconnect; it does not affect development SSH on 8022. `tx ssh keys-list` and the same read-only fingerprint view in TUI/Web/GTK show shared Termux account key type and label without returning key bytes; those keys may authorize both 8022 and 8023. Shared-account public-key enrollment and revocation now have exact preview/confirmation flows in CLI and Web; the TUI can select an owned Native .ssh/*.pub key or an authorized fingerprint. GTK controls, guided key generation/recovery, durable rollback, and per-service boot/Wake Lock policy remain open. Any key change affects both ports 8022 and 8023. No live key material or SSH configuration was changed during this source implementation. The deployment workflow `tx ssh deploy` shows a hash-bound diff; apply requires `--yes --plan-id` from that preview. Deployment preserves the running process and never restarts the service. Snapshot rollback is also preview-first (`tx ssh deploy-rollback-preview --operation-id ID`, then `tx ssh deploy-rollback --operation-id ID --yes --plan-id PLAN`). The separate owner-started 8022 development channel is not managed by this workflow. Process ownership/reboot qualification limitations are recorded in [8023 evidence](docs/evidence/2026-10-18-8023-reconciliation.md); see the [qualification plan](docs/testing/8023-deployment-and-lifecycle.md).
